renderPacket.identity: A real Havana city street with a recognizable mid-century blue American classic car in the foreground and the identifiable dome of El Capitolio in the distance; weathered pastel historic Havana facades and arcades, a coherent street-level perspective, restrained warm daylight, believable street alignment and historic architecture. Single wide composition for desktop and mobile crops, quiet watercolor with photographic place fidelity. No text, invented landmarks, panels or collage.

Real Viñales Valley in Pinar del Río, western Cuba: several isolated rounded steep limestone mogotes rise directly from a broad level cultivated valley, red-brown tobacco fields and modest low farmhouses, scattered royal palms, distant karst ridges. Human-height slightly elevated valley-floor viewpoint, clear soft daylight; no water, bay, cliff-side town or invented dramatic peaks. Single geographic place, authentic agriculture and subdued watercolor, 3:2 landscape.

Actual Ciénaga de Zapata in Matanzas, southern Cuba: low completely flat coastal freshwater and brackish wetland, shallow dark-green water channels between mangrove stands and tall pale marsh grasses, sparse scrub and a distant flat horizon. Low natural waterside viewpoint and soft overcast Caribbean daylight. A real wetland, not a turquoise waterfall, dramatic hill, wide beach or mountainous forest. One continuous 3:2 quiet watercolor landscape.

Real Parque José Martí in central Cienfuegos, Cuba: the spacious historic civic square with its recognizable white-and-cream neoclassical public buildings, Teatro Tomás Terry's low facade and the Palacio de Gobierno's red dome, orderly nineteenth-century streets and mature shade trees. Human-height coherent viewpoint looking across the square, warm diffuse daylight and realistically restrained architectural detail. No waterfront palace or ocean in this inland square; 3:2 quiet watercolor single scene.

Real Plaza Mayor in Trinidad Cuba: slightly sloping cobblestone colonial square, low pastel yellow and pale blue stucco buildings with terracotta tiled roofs, the recognizable cream Iglesia Parroquial de la Santísima Trinidad at the upper side of the square, wrought iron garden railing and royal palms, natural pedestrian-scale perspective. No invented giant tower or vast city boulevard. 3:2 soft Caribbean daylight, authentic quiet watercolor.

Real Playa Flamenco on Cayo Coco, low north-coast cay of Cuba: long pale fine sandy shore, shallow transparent turquoise Caribbean water grading toward deeper blue with subtle distant reef line, flat low dune scrub and sparse palms, low undeveloped horizon. Modest human-height oblique view along the beach with soft natural daylight, not an invented mountainous tropical island or a resort-filled coastline. One 3:2 quiet watercolor photographically credible view.

Historic centre of real Camagüey, Cuba: irregular narrow cobblestone streets bending around modest pastel one- and two-storey colonial homes, barred windows, sun-worn lime plaster and terracotta roof tiles, a small intimate neighborhood plaza and a traditional earthenware tinajón of realistic size. Coherent street-level viewpoint with a turning alley, no vast grand plaza or invented dominant cathedral. 3:2 restrained soft daylight watercolor.

Actual raised limestone marine terraces of Desembarco del Granma National Park around Cabo Cruz, southeast Cuba: repeated horizontal flat-topped limestone benches and sharp pale rock scarps stepped down toward open deep Caribbean Sea, sparse coastal scrub rooted in rock and breakers along the lowest rocky edge. Clear broad oblique coast view emphasizes geomorphic stair-steps. Not a harbor fortress, invented castle, sand beach or urban skyline. One coherent 3:2 quiet watercolor landscape.

Real Alejandro de Humboldt National Park in the humid Nipe-Sagua-Baracoa mountains of far-eastern Cuba: layered dense tropical evergreen forest canopy across rolling steep green hills and a narrow river valley, exceptionally lush endemic vegetation, mist-softened distant forest ridges and a natural dark clear stream at the valley floor. No coastal Baracoa town, El Yunque mountain landmark, waterfalls or invented resort. One coherent 3:2 daylight quiet watercolor of the inland protected forest.
